# Inkling 2 Mini: Introducing Inkling 2 Mini

English · [简体中文](../zh/tml-inkling-2-mini.md) · [Back to the list](../../README.md)

<sub>Thinking Machines Lab blog · 2026-11-20 · Thinking Machines Lab</sub>

<img src="../../assets/glyphs/tml-inkling-2-mini.svg" alt="L0-5 (6 layers) -&gt; [L6-17 (12 layers)] x 3 -&gt; L18-23 (6 layers); injection depth-attention; KV per-pass">

> Open-weight MoE (26.4B total, 3.4B active) that runs the middle 12 of its 24 layers three times with shared weights, released with a variable-loop research twin used to measure how pass count affects capability and CoT monitorability.

**Category**: Architecture: where to loop, what to share · **Status**: draft (numbers not yet re-checked) · **Impact**: HN points 1,482

[paper](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/) · [project](https://thinkingmachines.ai/model-card/inkling-2-mini/) · [blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/inkling2mini) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini)

## Problem

Looping lets a model do more serial computation per token without adding parameters, which has raised concerns that looped models are harder to oversee by reading their chain of thought; the post reports what looping gives a small open model and how pass count affects CoT monitorability.

## Method

- 24 MoE layers (8 of 128 experts per token) in four six-layer blocks; the two middle blocks share weights and run three times, giving 48 layer applications per token from 24 stored layers.
- Every pass starts from the prelude output; passes 2 and 3 also read the previous pass's middle-block outputs (the message) through attention residuals, and a learned gate that initially blocks the message lets looping be introduced stably during training.
- Training started with 8 of 384 experts per token; two-thirds of the experts were pruned at one point in midtraining (keeping the 128 most used per layer), followed by 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling model, SFT, and RL totaling 2.2T tokens over 2,000 steps. Expert layers use NVFP4 on all forward passes and the last four layers use MXFP8.
- A variable-loop research model, TML-d24-varloop-research, was trained with 1 to 5 passes (sampled 1:2:6:2:1 for the rest of midtraining, post-trained at 3) and is run at 1 to 5 passes, and at 10 in the no-CoT tests, to measure capability and CoT monitorability.

## Loop layout

| Facet | Value |
|---|---|
| Where the loop sits | middle core (prelude-core-coda) |
| Weight sharing | fully tied |
| Passes in training | fixed |
| Passes at test time | fixed |
| Input injection | attention over earlier passes |
| KV cache | per-pass KV |
| Gradient through passes | n/a |
| Origin | n/a |
| FFN | MoE |
| Attention in the loop | hybrid (full + window / linear) |
| Passes (L6-17) | train 3; test 3 |

Inkling 2 Mini has 24 MoE layers (8 of 128 experts per token) in four six-layer blocks; the two middle blocks share weights and run three times, so 24 stored layers give 48 layer applications per token. Per the Hugging Face blog, each block has five sliding-window layers (1,024-token window) and one full-attention layer, and each layer visit keeps its own KV. Every pass starts from the prelude output; passes 2 and 3 also read the previous pass's middle-block outputs (the message) through attention residuals, admitted by a learned gate that starts fully closed. Labels are 0-indexed as in the Hugging Face blog; the post numbers the same core 7-18. The released research twin TML-d24-varloop-research has the same layout but was trained with 1 to 5 passes and is run at up to 10 in the post.

## Other findings

- On the scaling ladder, an unpruned non-looping model cost 7.5% less compute to train than the unpruned looped version but needed 140% more inference compute to match its loss on 512k-token agentic traces. (Looping design)
- TML-d24-varloop-research was never trained with more than five passes, yet running it with ten does not significantly degrade its no-CoT time horizon (40 s, against 42 s at five), and on N-Hop Lookup it follows longer chains with more passes, improving out to ten loops. (No-CoT capabilities; figures "No-CoT time horizons" and "N-Hop Lookup")
- With CoT, more passes mainly help multi-hop reasoning rather than recall: gains are largest on long-context retrieval (MRCR), then math and science reasoning, then long-horizon agentic tasks, while knowledge-intensive benchmarks (AA-Omniscience, SimpleQA Verified, SimpleVQA, WorldVQA) do not improve with more passes. (Capabilities; No-CoT capabilities)
- Accuracy at each reasoning-token budget generally rises with passes, with diminishing returns after 3; on GPQA Diamond questions solved at all pass counts, reasoning at 5 passes averages 1,661 tokens against 3,703 at 1 pass, with unchanged sentence length and dictionary-word share. (CoT monitorability; Compression and legibility)
- Among CoTs of 750-1,250 tokens, Inkling 2 Mini and the variable-loop model at 3 passes follow a CoT instruction at most 0.1% of the time (Qwen3.8-27B 1.3%), too rarely to separate loop counts; LinuxArena stealth rates show no clear trend with the number of passes. (CoT monitorability (Controllability); Agentic monitorability)

## Comparison

- **Baseline**: A scaling-ladder run that loops the last 12 layers (13-24) instead of the middle 12 (7-18), with the same three passes and equal training compute; both runs' gains are expressed as the compute a no-loop baseline would need to match their loss.
- **Held fixed**: F (training FLOPs)
- **Differs**: none
- **Baseline hyperparameters**: not stated
- **Headline claim**: Looping the middle 12 layers gave larger accuracy gains than looping the last 12 on 27 of 28 evaluations; at training step 2,000 a no-loop baseline was estimated to need 1.51-1.91x the compute to match the middle loop's loss, against 1.24-1.36x for the last loop. (Looping design; figure "Compute-equivalent gain by loop position")

## Caveats

- Inkling 2 Mini supports only a fixed number of passes (3), so every pass-count comparison uses TML-d24-varloop-research, whose later training stages differ; its model card cautions against comparing it directly with Inkling 2 Mini.
- Three passes dominated the variable-loop model's training and its RL used 3 passes only; the authors say results at other pass counts may understate what dedicated training could achieve and do not show what RL at a higher pass count would learn.
- The loop-placement and looping-versus-non-looping comparisons come from scaling-ladder runs (placement at training step 2,000; unpruned models for looping versus non-looping), not from the released model, and the post does not give the sizes of those runs.
- No-CoT results use a subset of Think Fast tasks, with answers elicited by prefilling the start of the response; the models were not trained to answer without CoT.
- LinuxArena used a helpful-only fine-tune of Inkling 2 Mini, a weaker monitor (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) and a subset of 184 task pairings.
- Decoding speeds in the opening coding figure are theoretical ceilings (614 GB/s, BF16 weights, batch size one), evaluation setups vary by model, and the post gives no pretraining token count.
